correctness.rationale: Proof uses E(S)=q^{coverage}, exact subset Möbius inversion, and parity coefficient of the sole unknown coverage u(P)=N. Every feasible integer interval point gives a nonnegative incidence vector with sum N, and exactly recovers the measured proper-subset law; outside interval a type multiplicity is negative. The even/odd parity family proves lower marginal insufficiency for all m>=3. Three-plant bounds [6,8] are exact. Standalone independent arithmetic tests on 857 profiles and 7 parity examples reproduce the certificate; finite checks are not substituted for proof. Known q, exact moments, no empty latent columns explicitly assumed.

originality.rationale: A directly dominating complete-joint OR-mixture identifiability theorem was found and is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim (Nguyen and Zheng, arXiv:1007.0528, Sections III-IV). The new assessed statement instead classifies all missing-top-marginal OR-network incidence completions by an explicit sharp consecutive integer census interval and proves matching known-census lower-marginal obstruction. Full-text comparison and actual targeted database/literature searches did not find this exact incomplete-marginal classification; a general contingency-table parity characterization remains a genuine residual risk. Independent bibliographic checking is not performed.
residual_risks: Classical contingency-table / Boolean OR inverse results may include a general result implying the explicit census interval without the same ecological terminology.
The full-law identifiability theorem in Nguyen–Zheng is stronger for complete observations; the fixed-census uniqueness corollary by itself is not novel.
Partial bibliographic searching and a bounded number of primary papers cannot establish exhaustive noncoverage.

value.rationale: Complete feasible-census classification for a natural latent ecological interaction reconstruction problem from all proper coextinction marginals. It identifies precisely when missing the all-species extinction event leaves ambiguity, enumerates every possible pollinator census and every incidence network without gaps, shows a three-plant dataset with exactly three distinct networks, and proves the m−1 marginal-order cutoff sharp even with known census. These are structural identifiability facts and exact boundary counterexamples, not an arbitrary finite calculation or a purported extension of the covered full-data theorem.
